The main theorem covers arbitrary physical initial preparations, simultaneous
number-conserving hopping/density interactions, ordinary unscaled equal loss,
and calibrated sparse observation under a common implemented feedback policy.
It proves complete permitted RECORD accuracy, not physical-state trace
reconstruction from a classical mixture. Physical access, initial/controller
correlations, numerical precision and potentially exponential mode dependence
are retained. Historical novelty and practical superiority remain UNKNOWN.

The canonical physical Husimi law replaces the earlier purification-amplitude
diagonal. A backward-effect argument needs no derivatives of the preparation.
Ordinary loss bounds accumulated nonlinear sensitivity and the remaining count
budget. A separate heterodyne interface can acquire initial finite cell weights
and a probability-tail certificate; no such experiment was performed here.
This does not use P3's coherent-overlap verifier or establish that composition.

weak-interaction/weak-detection regime, it converges to the positive classical
law with BOTH amplitude damping and nonlinear phase accumulated along the
damped trajectory. Its relevant nonlinear clock is (1-exp(-dt))/d, rather than
t. A delayed observation window separates this phase correction from merely
getting the decaying intensity right.

  TV(exact quantum record, correct damped nonlinear limit) <= 0.000538488;
  TV(exact quantum record, correct damping but old phase clock) >= 0.072192509;
  TV(exact quantum record, unchanged old weak-bath law) >= 0.280862244.
These are three-outcome record statements, not distances between quantum states.
There is also an exact comparison of two physical models, with Kerr switched
on versus off: their COMPLETE POOLED count path laws coincide, while their
mixed-output first-port records have TV in [0.0399618297,0.0402409160].
The exact dyadic interval is in the JSON.

Exact damped Kerr dynamics has strong established predecessors. The present
role is an acceptance test for the proposed general open-system record law,
with supplied preparation, kinetics and measurement access. It is not a claim

The unscaled-bath direction yields a closed positive predictor for interacting bosonic systems under appreciable loss, initialized from the physical preparation’s Husimi distribution. It predicts the complete permitted record under feedback, with an explicit quantum error allowance.

The main advance over the preceding construction is that no smoothness assumption on a preparation amplitude or purification kernel is needed. The proof transfers the regularity requirement to future record probabilities, where the dynamics and observation rule control it.

The retained variable is a probability law of current relative coherence, together with the actual controller. This is a substantial distribution, rather than a universally small set of moments. Its finite representation has a paid cost. In the regime proved here, that cost is governed by the accessible readouts, the preparation’s phase-space tails, and accumulated nonlinear sensitivity relative to loss.
